note: Spoken callnames through the game's audio service (docs/callnames.md section 5, turbogui/src/core/commentary_audio.h). Same entries as the built-in table in turbogui/src/core/sigscan.cpp. Check with: bash scripts/re/py.sh scripts/re/verify_callnames.py. Several entries share one pattern and differ by offset: the resolver reads the rip-relative instruction at match + offset, so the strings come out as the game's own constants.

commentary_service_registry.note: the Create Player list reader 0x1480B2128 loads the service registry pointer here before GetCommentaryService; [slot] = the registry (1,117 code references in the image)

commentary_service_get.note: void** GetCommentaryService(void** out, Registry*): registry->vcall(0x40)(0xA621C80) then entry->vcall(0x18)(0xA621C86) (returns the entry itself, 0x142899DF4); the caller releases through the service's vcall 0x8 (lock xadd -1 on service+0x10)

commentary_filter_names.note: void FilterNames(Inner*, eastl::vector<{int row, int commentaryid}>*): bridge = [inner+0x10]->vcall(0xE0)("CommentaryBridge"); ctx = audio->vcall(0x48)("CommentaryDbEvents", "PLAYER_NAME_FE"); one SpeechQuery {player_intensity = 2}; per element surname_ID = id, bridge->vcall(0xB8)(query), erase in place on false. Reached by the game through names vtable slot 24 (0x1438AEE38: this+8 -> inner)

speech_query_ctor.note: SpeechQuery* ctor(SpeechQuery* q, ScratchScope* scope, EventCtx* ctx): q+0 vtable 0x149621F80, +0x10/+0x38/+0x68 scope, +0x18 param count, +0x20..0x30 param array, +0x48 0x14BCAD848, +0x50 1, +0x58 1.0f, +0x5C 2.0f, +0x80 0; ctx != null -> 0x1407B0F3C(q, ctx). Object 0x84 bytes

speech_query_set_int.note: void SetInt(SpeechQuery*, const char* name, int): 0x1407AEF2C hashes the name (djb2-xor) and finds the parameter index; an existing parameter is overwritten, else one is added from the scope

scratch_scope_ctor.note: ScratchScope* ctor(ScratchScope*): vtable 0x14960E268, +0x18 the thread's scratch allocator (0x140539FD4), +0x28/+0x30 its saved position; 0x40 bytes. Destroyed in LIFO order by scratch_scope_dtor

scratch_scope_dtor.note: void ~ScratchScope(this): rewinds the allocator to the saved position

commentary_service_vtable.note: CommentaryService vtable from its constructor 0x1438A145C (the only other reference: 0x1438A253B). Slot 1 (0x8) Release 0x141D4281C, slot 3 (0x18) QueryInterface 0x142899DF4 (ids 0xEE3F516E / 0xA621C86 -> this), slot 12 (0x60) 0x1438A59A0 = [this+0x40]

commentary_names_vtable.note: vtable of the names object the service constructor allocates (0x140670D24) and stores at service+0x40, with +0x08 = null until the audio binds it. Slot 24 (0xC0) 0x1438AEE38 = FilterNames([this+8], vector) when [this+8] != null

commentary_str_player_low_simple.note: "PLAYER_LOW_SIMPLE": inside the frontend per-player check 0x14294A0F4 (int GetCallname(this, int playerid, int mode): -1 when PLAYER_LOW_SIMPLE / PLAYER_LOW_LINK have audio for player_db_pID = playerid, else the playernamemap id when PLAYER_NAME_FE has it, else the name ids' commentary id); its only caller is 0x1438EB8B0, so Turbo builds the queries itself

layout.names+0x08: inner object FilterNames takes (null while the audio is not bound)
layout.inner+0x10: audio system: vcall 0xE0 GetSubsystem(name), vcall 0x48 GetEventContext(category, event)
layout.CommentaryBridge vtable 0x14A8DC8C0: slot 23 (0xB8) HasAudio(SpeechQuery*) -> 0x14294FCA0 -> 0x1444F340C (event registry at SpeechSystem+0x50, handler 0x1414A9D14, event lookup by name 0x1414AAEF4: a linear strcmp over the 10,201 base-db events, which is why Turbo budgets its batches per frame)
layout.vector element: u64: low 32 bits = row (position), high 32 bits = commentaryid (FilterNames reads +4)
